paragraph: In January 2026 the Banco Nacional de Angola issued [Aviso 1/26](<https://lex.ao/docs/banco-nacional-de-angola/2026/aviso-n-o-1-26-de-28-de-janeiro/>), which lets only payment companies it has authorised act as non-bank acquirers. [Expansão reports the BNA launched the Kwik instant-payment platform in June 2023](<https://www.expansao.co.ao/angola/detalhe/movimentos-entre-carteiras-digitais-valem-apenas-06-no-kwik-74789.html>). In the last twelve months, [the BNA joined the kwanza to the SADC-RTGS from 27 July 2026, with five Angolan banks taking part](<https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/mundo/3030615/angola-elimina-intermediarios-em-pagamentos-entre-paises-da-sadc>). No source found since October 2023 says Angola is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Angolan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[The BRB launched BurundiPay, the national instant payment system, on 23 April 2026](<https://www.brb.bi/node/3303>), and is its promoter. [By 4 August 2026, 17 institutions were live on it](<https://www.jimberemag.org/une-revolution-de-leconomie-digitale-au-burundi/>). [The BRB's 2024 report on payment systems names the e-money issuers it had licensed at end-September 2024](<https://www.brb.bi/sites/default/files/2025-11/Rapport%20annuel%20sur%20les%20syst%C3%A8mes%20et%20moyens%20de%20%20paiement%20et%20leur%20surveillance.pdf>): Saisai Fintech, Lumicash and Ellis Business Company. In the last twelve months, [the BRB moved its Automated Transfer System to ISO 20022 in February 2026](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundi-upgrades-payment-system-to-international-iso-20022-standard/>). No source found since October 2023 says Burundi is live on PAPSS, and joining does not count. Mature would need Burundian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[BCEAO launched PI-SPI on 30 September 2025 as a 24/7 interoperable instant payment platform for the UEMOA](<https://bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/connexion-la-plateforme-interoperable-du-systeme-de-paiement-instantane-pi-spi-de>). In the last twelve months, [its communique reports 80 participants connected on 2 April 2026](<https://bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/connexion-la-plateforme-interoperable-du-systeme-de-paiement-instantane-pi-spi-de>). [A BCEAO notice of 2 October 2026 makes PI-SPI compulsory for interoperable e-money transfers](<https://triomphemag.com/interoperabilite-du-mobile-money-au-benin-pi-spi-entre-en-vigueur-ce-qui-change-reellement-pour-les-utilisateurs-des-ce-2-novembre/>), from 2 November 2026. [Four payment institutions held a BCEAO licence in Benin at 31 August 2026](<https://beninwebtv.bj/benin-quatre-etablissements-paiement-agrees-aout-2026/>). No source found since October 2023 says Benin is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Beninese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[LeFaso.net reports that the BCEAO launched the PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform on 30 September 2025](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article147670>). In the last twelve months, [the BCEAO had 80 institutions connected by 24 June 2026](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article147670>). [As of 24 February 2026 it had authorised nine institutions in Burkina Faso to offer PI-SPI instant payment services to the public](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article144889>), including Orange Money, Coris Bank International and Ecobank. No source found since October 2023 says Burkina Faso is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Burkinabe banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

The Bank of Botswana says [the Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, have been in effect since 2 April 2026](<https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/press-release-files/Implementation%20of%20the%20Electronic%20Payment%20Services%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%2C%202026.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [no one may operate an electronic payment service without its licence](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/bob-electronic-money-regulations-gather-pace/news>). The penalty is a P1 million fine or five years in prison. The Bank said the National Payments Switch Act has been [drafted, with no tabling date](<https://www.bwtechzone.com/2025/07/national-payments-switch-act-drafted.html>). No source found since October 2023 says the central bank runs or oversees a national switch. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

In November 2023 AfricaNenda said [BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent](<https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf>). The switch serves payment providers in the Central African Republic. In the last twelve months, [PAPSS said BEAC joined PAPSS on 9 July 2026](<https://papss.com/media/beac-joins-papss-connecting-payments-between-cemac-and-the-rest-of-africa/>). In April 2026 the UMAC ministerial committee [validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard](<https://leconomie.info/article/paiement-numerique-le-gimac-officialise-la-norme-qr-code-interoperable-de-la-cemac>), and it was launched over GIMACPAY on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the country is live on PAPSS. Joining does not count. Mature would need banks or payment providers in the country to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

In September 2025 the BCEAO [granted licence EME.CI.025/2025 to Djogana Pay for its Peya Pay e-money](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2637099/economie/inclusion-financieremonnaie-electronique-la-cote-divoire-enregistre-un-4e-etablissement>). It [launched its PI-SPI instant payment platform on 30 September 2025](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2641755/economie/uemoa-linteroperabilite-des-paiements-devient-obligatoire-des-le-30-juin-2026>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, it said [Cote d'Ivoire's Treasury was already connected](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/connexion-des-tresors-publics-la-plateforme-interoperable-du-systeme-de-paiement>). Since 2 November 2026 [interoperable e-money transfers must route through it](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/11/03/failed-transfers-hidden-fees-and-phantom-aliases-inside-the-messy-birth-of-west-africas-unified-payments-network/>). Nothing found since October 2023 shows the country live on PAPSS. Joining PAPSS, or a regional payment system, does not count. Mature would need Ivorian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[GIMACPAY has been in service since 2021](<https://leconomie.info/article/paiement-numerique-le-gimac-officialise-la-norme-qr-code-interoperable-de-la-cemac>), and [BEAC publishes its figures](<https://lejour.cm/mobile-money-gimacpay-franchit-la-barre-des-600-milliards-fcfa-de-transactions/>). In the last twelve months, [BEAC launched the interoperable CEMAC QR code on 29 July 2026 in Douala](<https://www.gabonreview.com/cemac-moins-de-cash-plus-de-numerique-la-beac-deploie-le-qr-code-interoperable/>). [It rests on Regulation 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/COREFI of 8 April 2026](<https://www.gabonreview.com/cemac-moins-de-cash-plus-de-numerique-la-beac-deploie-le-qr-code-interoperable/>), and covers the six CEMAC countries, cleared through GIMAC. No source found since October 2023 says Cameroon is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Cameroonian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[The Banque Centrale du Congo's map of the national payment system](<https://www.bcc.cd/intermediaires-financiers/systemes-de-paiement/infrastructures>) lists, at end-2023, 15 banks and other credit institutions, 81 money-transfer firms and five other financial companies. [Bankable reports that Switch Mosolo is the national payment switch developed under the Central Bank of Congo's oversight](<https://bankable.africa/en/news/1409-3591-drc-microfinance-institutions-seek-digital-support-ahead-of-dollar-cash-ban>). In the last twelve months, [an agreement signed on 15 April 2026 connected microfinance institutions and savings cooperatives to the national card switch](<https://actualite.cd/2026/04/16/rdc-le-projet-transforme-appuie-la-digitalisation-des-imf-et-coopec>). [Le Point CD reports that the central bank joined PAPSS in September 2026](<https://lepoint.cd/paiements-transfrontaliers-le-papss-ouvre-son-reseau-aux-banques-et-fintechs-de-la-rdc/>). Banks and fintechs were invited to apply on 21 October 2026. Mature would need Congolese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, provides interoperable payment services to providers in the six CEMAC states](<https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf>), including the Republic of Congo. It says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent. In the last twelve months, [the UMAC ministerial committee validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard in April 2026, and it was launched on 29 July 2026 over GIMACPAY](<https://leconomie.info/article/paiement-numerique-le-gimac-officialise-la-norme-qr-code-interoperable-de-la-cemac>). No source found since October 2023 says Congo is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Congolese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

The Banque Centrale des Comores' [financial inclusion strategy](<https://banque-comores.km/article/show/strategie-nationale-dinclusion-financiere-20252030>) cites its regulation no. 1 of 2017 on e-money institutions. That regulation sets the licensing terms for e-money issuers. The BCC [operates, supervises and takes part in KomorPay](<https://banque-comores.km/uploads/BCC-livret(3).pdf>), the interbank payment system, which has run since 23 April 2026. In the last twelve months, Al-Watwan reports the BCC [launched Komor Switch](<https://alwatwan.net/economie/secteur-bancaire-i-les-comores-inaugurent-de-nouveaux-modes-et-syst%C3%A8mes-de-paiement.html>). It links all banks and mobile money services. No source found since October 2023 says the Comoros takes part in PAPSS. Mature would need Comorian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[The Banco de Cabo Verde says it manages SICIL, the interbank clearing system for cheques, credit transfers and payment cards](<https://www.bcv.cv/pt/SistemadePagamentos/Paginas/SistemadePagamentos.aspx>), and requires payment institutions and e-money institutions to be authorised by it. [In 2024 it continued revising the legal framework for payment services and the issuance of electronic money](<https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2025/Relat%C3%B3rio%20de%20Sistema%20de%20Pagamentos%202024.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Cape Verde takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Cape Verde live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

[The Banque Centrale de Djibouti's 2024 annual report says no institution may offer financial services without its licence](<https://banque-centrale.dj/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Rapport-Annuel_-V.Definitive.pdf>). It names two e-money issuers it oversees, D-Money and WAAFI. [The same report says its automated clearing house has run since October 2022](<https://banque-centrale.dj/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Rapport-Annuel_-V.Definitive.pdf>). [AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2024 says Djibouti had integrated with PAPSS](<https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips-2024-mainreport-EN.pdf>), and it was then unclear whether retail transactions were processed. In the last twelve months, [PAPSS's June 2026 coverage sheet lists Djibouti as a country with live send-and-receive participants](<https://papss.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/PAPSS-PAYMENTS-NETWORK-COVERAGE_JUNE2026-5.pdf>): East African Bank and Salaam African Bank. [Its November 2026 sheet still lists Djibouti](<https://papss.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/PAPSS-PAYMENTS-NETWORK-COVERAGE_NOVEMBER2026.pdf>).

In August 2025 [Launchbase Africa reported](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2025/08/19/algeria-opens-for-fintech-new-psp-rules-create-a-playbook-for-payments-startups/>) that Bank of Algeria Instruction 06-2025 requires payment service providers to join the national payment and clearing systems, which the Bank oversees. The report names no switch. In the last twelve months, [a banking consultant said in March 2026](<https://care.dz/fr/espace-presse/prestataires-de-services-de-paiement-le-rappel-a-lordre-dun-banquier-art752>) that the Bank had licensed no provider under its Regulation 25-02. On 23 September 2026 the Bank's Monetary and Banking Council [authorised Djezzy Payment Services to set up as a payment service provider](<https://ecotimesdz.com/djezzy-payment-services-psp-banque-algerie-paiement-mobile-2026/>). No source found since October 2023 names a national switch or retail clearing system the Bank runs. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

[The CBE says its InstaPay instant payments network had over 16 million users and 1.1 billion transactions by June 2025](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5335311.aspx>). [InstaPay runs through the bank's Instant Payment Network, the national real-time payment infrastructure](<https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/576342.aspx>). [The Central Bank of Egypt agreed to join PAPSS in November 2024](<https://enterpriseam.com/egypt/2026/09/23/instapay-to-connect-with-pan-african-payment-system-as-six-egyptian-banks-apply-for-integration/>). In the last twelve months, [six Egyptian banks applied to the CBE for final approvals to integrate with PAPSS](<https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/576342.aspx>), and in September 2026 they were still applying. No source found reports Egyptian payments running on PAPSS. Mature would need Egyptian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS; joining does not count.

[In 2025 Himbol's guide said Himbol operates under the supervision and licensing of the Bank of Eritrea](<https://erihimbol.com/assets/Himbol%20-%20Customers%20and%20Partners%20Guide-CrBqoCzf.pdf>). [Himbol runs the M-Nakfa mobile wallet and remittance payout](<https://erihimbol.com/assets/Himbol%20-%20Customers%20and%20Partners%20Guide-CrBqoCzf.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the central bank runs or oversees a national switch. None says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

In May 2023 the National Bank of Ethiopia [gave Safaricom M-PESA a Payment Instrument Issuer licence](<https://onafriq.com/press/article/m-pesa-safaricom-partners-with-onafriq-enabling-the-flow-of-remittances-to-ethiopia>). On 12 May 2025 it [raised the minimum capital of these issuers from 50 million to 100 million birr](<https://birrmetrics.com/ethiopia-doubles-capital-threshold-for-mobile-money-providers-as-central-bank-tightens-grip-on-digital-finance/>), and that month it [made interoperability among mobile wallets mandatory](<https://ethiopianmonitor.com/2025/05/27/nbe-mandates-interoperability-among-mobile-wallets/>). In the last twelve months, on 15 October 2026, the Bank and PAPSS [announced that Ethiopia had joined the PAPSS network](<https://www.afreximbank.com/ethiopia-joins-papss-network-as-national-bank-of-ethiopia-and-papss-announce-the-2nd-edition-of-cowry-in-addis-ababa/>). In October 2026 the Capital newspaper reported that the Bank [licenses ETTA's ZooryaPay as a payment system operator](<https://capitalethiopia.com/2026/10/07/ethiopias-commerce-goes-contactless-with-new-visa-and-etta-infrastructure-agreement/>). No source found says Ethiopian banks or payment providers send and receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need that to be live.

[BEAC launched the interoperable CEMAC QR code on 29 July 2026 in Douala](<https://www.gabonreview.com/cemac-moins-de-cash-plus-de-numerique-la-beac-deploie-le-qr-code-interoperable/>). [It rests on Regulation 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/COREFI of 8 April 2026](<https://www.gabonreview.com/cemac-moins-de-cash-plus-de-numerique-la-beac-deploie-le-qr-code-interoperable/>). [AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent](<https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf>), a switch that serves Gabon. The QR code is the one change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Gabon is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Gabonese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[The Bank of Ghana's head of fintech said in October 2026 that the Bank set up GhIPSS in 2007](<https://channelonenewsonline.com/2026/10/22/bank-of-ghana-pushes-for-seamless-african-cross-border-payments/>). [GhIPSS is a publicly owned national payment infrastructure that connects banks, mobile money operators and other payment providers](<https://channelonenewsonline.com/2026/10/22/bank-of-ghana-pushes-for-seamless-african-cross-border-payments/>). In the last twelve months, [the Governor launched SaoPay as a new Dedicated Electronic Money Issuer on 7 October 2026](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/REMARKS-BY-GOVERNOR-DR-JOHNSON-PANDIT-ASIAMA-AT-THE-OFFICIAL-LAUNCH-OF-SAOPAY-091026.pdf>). Governor Asiama said the Bank has [extended PAPSS to mobile wallets in the Ghana-Nigeria corridor](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/ghana-news-ghana-rwanda-nigeria-test-new-cross-border-digital-payment-systems.html>). In November 2026 the Governor said [the Bank is developing a legal and regulatory framework for fintech companies](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/11/bog-develops-open-banking-framework-to-facilitate-customer-data-sharing/>).

[In July 2026 the central bank and Guinéenne de Monétique had built NimbaPay, a national instant payment platform](<https://focusguinee.info/2026/07/26/laguiduten-salue-le-lancement-de-nimbapay-la-plateforme-nationale-de-paiement-instantane/>). [The BCRG's supervision director general said the central bank is putting NimbaPay into operation](<https://mediaguinee.com/2026/07/paiements-digitaux-ofmg-la-cciag-et-la-bcrg-engagent-une-demarche-pour-encourager-les-transactions-electroniques-en-guinee/>). It links banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, [the bank was preparing a payment systems law and a payments strategy for 2027-2030](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites/2610-142742-guinee-nimbapay-traite-7-6-millions-de-transactions-et-connecte-7-etablissements-en-4-mois>), Agence Ecofin reports. No source found since October 2023 says Guinea takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Guinea live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

[The Point says the central bank co-led the launch of BANTABA 2.0, the country's first real-time interoperable payment system, in December 2025](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/gambia-launches-bantaba-2-0-first-real-time-interoperable-payment-system>). [Gamswitch says the central bank gave regulatory leadership and oversight for the switch](<https://www.gamswitch.com/press-release/the-gambia-launches-bantaba-2-0-its-first-real-time-interoperable-payment-system>). [The Digital Cooperation Organization's 2025 Gambia report says mobile money providers must be authorised by the central bank](<https://dco.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Gambia-Report.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [the central bank launched a National Payment Systems Advisory Committee after BANTABA 2.0 went live](<https://www.gamswitch.com/press-release/the-gambia-launches-national-payment-systems-advisory-committee-npsac-to-strengthen-payment-system-governance>). [PAPSS's June 2026 coverage sheet lists the Gambia as a country with live send-and-receive participants](<https://papss.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/PAPSS-PAYMENTS-NETWORK-COVERAGE_JUNE2026-5.pdf>), naming seven banks.

[The BCEAO runs PI-SPI, the instant payment platform for UEMOA members including Guinea-Bissau](<https://www.forbesafrica.com/current-affairs/2026/10/07/interoperability-not-truly-free-fintech-experts-on-west-africas-instant-payments-rollout>), launched on 30 September 2025. [The BCEAO's list of payment institutions licensed under Instruction n°001-01-2024 shows one in Guinea-Bissau, INTOUCH Guinée-Bissau, licensed 25 June 2025](<https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees-dans-lumoa-au-31-aout-2026>). In the last twelve months, [the BCEAO said Guinea-Bissau had 5 institutions authorised on PI-SPI at 31 July 2026](<https://financesao.com/uemoa-pi-spi-atteint-104-etablissements-autorises/>). No source found since October 2023 says Guinea-Bissau is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Bissau-Guinean banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

In November 2023 AfricaNenda said [BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent](<https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf>). The switch serves payment providers in Equatorial Guinea. In the last twelve months, [PAPSS said BEAC joined PAPSS on 9 July 2026](<https://papss.com/media/beac-joins-papss-connecting-payments-between-cemac-and-the-rest-of-africa/>). In April 2026 the UMAC ministerial committee [validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard](<https://leconomie.info/article/paiement-numerique-le-gimac-officialise-la-norme-qr-code-interoperable-de-la-cemac>), and it was launched over GIMACPAY on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the country is live on PAPSS. Joining does not count. Mature would need banks or payment providers in the country to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

[The Central Bank of Kenya regulates Kenswitch, a domestic payment switch](<https://www.business-standard.com/content/press-releases-ani/kenswitch-partners-with-payu-s-wibmo-to-strengthen-online-card-security-in-kenya-126110200460_1.html>), its November 2026 release says. [The CBK's directory of 6 November 2025 lists 41 authorised payment service providers](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Directory-of-Authorized-Payment-Service-Providers-6-November-2025.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the CBK and the National Treasury [published a draft National Payment System Policy and Bill, 2026](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/2026/09/21/draft-national-payment-system-policy-and-national-payment-system-bill-2026/>). In November 2026 the PAPSS chief executive [said KCB Group and Equity Bank are connected to the network](<https://capitalfm.africa/papss-bets-on-local-currencies-to-unlock-kenyas-africa-trade/>). No source found says Kenyan banks send payments out through PAPSS. Mature would need Kenyan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through it.

[The central bank launched Pay Na-Na, the country's first instant payment system, on 16 December 2025](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/west-africa-leans-towards-three-country-plan-for-regional-payment-system-liberia-central-bank-chief-says/>). It links the two mobile money operators. [CBL Directive 002/2025 applies to all licensed Mobile Money Providers](<https://cbl.org.lr/sites/default/files/documents/NEPS-IIPS%20Directive%20-%20092325.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the Governor said [banks and fintechs were still being brought onto Pay Na-Na](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/business/cbl-outlines-four-priorities-to-transform-liberia-s-digital-payment-system/article_39f669bb-c385-4c6e-a854-e9f6581fc1e6.html>). [The central bank is the settlement agent for PAPSS, launched in Liberia on 27 March 2025](<https://www.cbl.org.lr/media/features-articles/eg-saamoi-speaks-joint-launch-fined-papss-monrovia>). In November 2026 the Executive Governor said [Liberian traders' payments to Nigeria and Ghana are settled through PAPSS](<https://nairametrics.com/2026/11/18/nigeria-ghana-proposed-as-hosts-for-ecowas-regional-payment-system/>).

The central bank [runs the LYPay and OnePay instant payment services](<https://cbl.gov.ly/en/instant-payment-services-statistics/>), launched in 2024. On 31 July 2025 it said it [was paying public salaries into commercial bank accounts over its own instant payment network](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/485074>). In the last twelve months, in March 2026, it [told banks to switch on LYPay QR payments at point-of-sale devices](<https://libyaherald.com/2026/03/aldabaiba-government-and-cbl-take-further-actions-to-encourage-increased-e-payments-use-cbl-reduces-new-fx-bureaux-commission>) by 8 March. It also [joined PAPSS at the end of December 2025](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/pan-african-payment-settlement-system_papss-papss-papss-activity-7412119263794208768-y9NP>). No Libyan bank is reported live on PAPSS. Mature would need Libyan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS; joining does not count.

[From 11 May 2025 the Central Bank of Lesotho and leading banks routed local card payments at shops through LeSwitch, the national switch](<https://publiceyenews.com/2025/05/20/leswitch-expands-to-pos-transactions>). [Boursenews reported in May 2025 that Switch Al-Maghrib, the national switch, is under the Bank's direct and continuous oversight](<https://boursenews.ma/article/marches/SWAM-une-nouvelle-identite-pour-piloter-la-souverainete-numerique-des-paiements>). [Bénin Web TV reports, from the BCEAO list, that Mali has two licensed payment institutions at 31 August 2026](<https://beninwebtv.bj/benin-quatre-etablissements-paiement-agrees-aout-2026/>). In the last twelve months, [the Bank launched the Metix instant payment system on 16 March 2026, run by SIMO](<https://360mozambique.com/economy/banking/metix-instant-payment-system-surpasses-11000-daily-transfers/>). Mature would need Mozambican banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

In the last twelve months, on 30 September 2026, the Reserve Bank [granted the local fintech PayChangu Limited](<https://malawi24.com/2026/10/17/payment-hurdles-ease-for-businesses/>) payment service provider licence PSP-003/26.
